clue.text: Beauty instrument has to be keen

parts.note: good looks are a person's beauty
the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A tool of the beauty trade needs a sharp edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To look sharp is to be alert and quick off the mark, which is being keen and eager.

clue.text: Tree line's a curved form

parts.note: an arch is a curved structure or shape

explanation.surface: A line of a tree's outline is a gentle curve.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, a familiar kind of tree.

clue.text: Ready to wear, despite falling from line?

definitions.text: Ready to wear, despite falling from line?

parts.words: Ready to wear, despite falling from line?
parts.note: clothes bought ready-made are said to come from a peg, and the joke pictures washing that has dropped off the clothes peg on the washing line yet is still fit to wear

explanation.surface: Laundry that blew off the washing line can still be worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought ready-made, not tailored, are described with this idiom from the shop rail.

clue.text: Isn't Josephine appearing in hospital drama?

indicators.note: one group of letters is shown within another, so these words set the first pieces inside the hospital word

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
Jo is a short form of the name Josephine

explanation.surface: An actress named Josephine is not starring in a television hospital drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hospital drama' suggests TV medical soaps, but the definition is just 'drama': SAINT JOAN is George Bernard Shaw's play about Joan of Arc.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play about Joan of Arc is a well-known stage drama.

clue.text: One newly-delivered oratorio

definitions.meaning: a baby just born is a youngster of the present age
a large-scale choral work, here the title of Michael Tippett's 1941 oratorio

explanation.definitionFit: Tippett's oratorio has this title, and a newborn is literally a youngster of the present era.

clue.text: Celebrate by camouflaging pillar-boxes?

definitions.meaning: to go out and celebrate wildly
British postboxes are already red, so painting the town that colour would hide them

explanation.walkthrough: PILLAR-BOXES are the red street postboxes of Britain. 'by' just links the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out on the town and celebrate extravagantly.

clue.text: Church article in due course reversing confusion

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the word for in due course is turned back to front

parts.note: so, in the sense 'and then', marks what follows in due course

explanation.surface: A church paper turns things round over time and causes confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is utter disorder, a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Bureaucracy nicely absorbs jaded person

indicators.note: the phrase takes the answer into itself, so it sits inside the run of these two words

explanation.surface: Red tape smoothly soaks up a weary sceptic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic is someone weary and distrustful of others' motives, a jaded type.

clue.text: Pictures almost completely a hit, except last page

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for completely is dropped

parts.note: all means completely, as in all gone

indicators.note: except signals removal, and last says the letter goes from the end of the word for a hit

parts.note: a bump is a knock or blow

explanation.surface: A photo collection is nearly all hits, apart from the final page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ALL to AL; 'except last page' drops P from BUMP, leaving BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book of photographs, a collection of pictures.

clue.text: Point to weapon man carried in various parades

indicators.note: one piece is borne inside the other, so the man word goes within the rearranged letters
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of parades are reworked

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A soldier points out his weapon while marching in assorted parades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' alone looks like the definition, but the whole phrase 'Point to weapon' is: the head of a spear is its point.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is literally the pointed tip of a spear, the weapon's point.

clue.text: Both fliers and swimmers smart

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is made up of fliers
fish are swimmers

explanation.surface: Pilots and fish alike are described as stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both' and 'and' only link the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means flashily or rakishly stylish, a looser sense of smart.

clue.text: Debased? I sadly belong among such people

definitions.text: Debased? I sadly belong among such people

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or regrettably, so the letters are put in a sorry new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses, with regret, that they belong among degraded people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges I and BELONG; the whole clue describes the speaker's lowly company.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means base or dishonourable, and originally of humble birth, so debased.

clue.text: Accompaniment to drum beat receives hand? Not half

indicators.note: the word for beat takes something into it, so it holds the other piece

parts.note: to hit is to beat

indicators.note: only half the word for hand is kept, so its second half goes

explanation.surface: A drumbeat gets a round of applause, though only a lukewarm one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like the slang for 'very much', but here it keeps only half of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-hat is a pair of cymbals played with the drum kit, accompanying the drums.

clue.text: Eye one initially appearing during Debussy piece?

definitions.text: Eye one initially appearing during Debussy piece?

indicators.note: something shown during a piece of music sits within it, so these letters go inside the work's title

parts.note: La Mer is an orchestral work by Claude Debussy
a private eye is a detective, a tec

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A detective turns up halfway through a performance of Debussy.
explanation.walkthrough: La Mer is Debussy's orchestral seascape. The whole clue also defines: someone turning up mid-performance has arrived late.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who appears while a piece is already being played has arrived late.

clue.text: Joint work brought back large African creature

parts.note: the hip is a joint

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the word for work is read in reverse

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A joint work brought back a big animal from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus, a hippo for short, is a huge African mammal.

clue.text: Reptile circles nude, cut off

parts.note: hoops are rings or circles

indicators.note: the word for nude loses its final letter

parts.note: naked means nude

explanation.surface: A snake rings an unclothed figure and is then severed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoop snake is a creature of American folklore said to roll like a wheel, a supposed reptile.

clue.text: Their woes should be re-expressed in a different way

indicators.note: expressing the letters again in another form calls for a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone's complaints ought to be phrased differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means differently or in another manner.

clue.text: Ripe fruit prepared, cored and pured, containing energy

annotationWithheld.why: Ripe fruit prepared, cored and puréed, containing energy (3,6): no parse found; 'prepared' with its middle removed and rearranged round E cannot supply the three Ps of RED PEPPER, and no search gives the setter's intent
annotationWithheld.clue: Ripe fruit prepared, cored and pured, containing energy

clue.text: Tone of voice suggesting long forgotten disease?

indicators.note: forgotten says a piece is left out of the word for tone of voice

parts.note: inflection is the rise and fall of the voice
L is the abbreviation for long, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A tone of voice hints at an illness that was long forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suggesting' is a link word; the question mark admits that an infection is a cause of disease rather than one itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An infection is the invasion of the body by germs, loosely a disease.

clue.text: Part of church ramshackle for a long time

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A church has been in poor repair for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ loft is the gallery in a church where the organ stands.

clue.text: Changed colour, having put foot in it in part of Wales

indicators.note: with in it, this tells us a piece is placed into the word for changed colour
it refers back to the dyeing word, which receives the extra letter

parts.note: dyed means changed in colour

explanation.surface: Someone who blushed after a gaffe in a Welsh region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put foot in it' looks like the idiom for a blunder, but it is the instruction to set F inside DYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyfed is a former county in south-west Wales, so a part of that country.

clue.text: Tie lined with green

parts.note: scored means marked with lines
raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A tie edged with green fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCORE DRAW in British football pools is a draw in which both teams score.
explanation.definitionFit: A score draw is a drawn match with goals, so a tie.

clue.text: Men welcoming Greek character in Biblical land

indicators.note: the men word takes in a guest, so it holds the other piece

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for soldiers who are not officers
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Soldiers greet a Greek in a land from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophir is the land of gold to which Solomon's ships sailed in the Bible.

clue.text: Painter among modernists, if one disregarded

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so the letter for one is dropped
the letters sit inside the word modernists

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One painter stands out in a group of modern artists, if one ignores the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Dada and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Be the best letters to represent 40, we hear

indicators.note: the words point to how the letters sound when said out loud

parts.note: XL is 40 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone trying to work out which letters stand for forty.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass others, to be the best.

clue.text: Say, in story: "Lord"

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A tale quotes a character addressing a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord, owed allegiance by vassals.

clue.text: Ghanaian tribe remains opposed

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
anti means opposed

explanation.surface: A tribe in Ghana continues to object.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are a people of central Ghana with a historic kingdom.

clue.text: Note piano has to come up in later musical statement

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to rise is to come up

explanation.surface: A piano note must rise later in a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated passage or theme returning later in a piece.

clue.text: Bird, say — tailless seabird, on reflection

parts.note: eg means for example, say

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the shortened seabird is reversed
the seabird loses its last letter

parts.note: the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reconsiders a seabird missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts TERN to TER; 'on reflection' turns it into RET.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Run and run in end of the second half of race, showing stamina

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word the
run is a word for disorder or loose movement, so the letters of the first two words are scattered
takes the latter half of the word race

explanation.surface: A runner keeps going to the end of the second half of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' rearranges RUN AND into NDURAN. 'in' and 'showing' only link. The first 'Run' is fodder, the second the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is staying power, the capacity to keep going, which is stamina.
